mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai Kona Electric engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned or rebuilt electric drive unit for the Hyundai Kona Electric typically ranges from £2,800 to £6,500 for supply only, depending on the 100kW or 150kW variant and condition.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of electric drive unit failure in a Hyundai Kona Electric?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early signs include a metallic whining or grinding noise from the front axle, especially under acceleration, loss of propulsion power, or inverter overheating warnings.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai Kona Electric?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the high retained value of the Kona Electric (typically £12,000-£25,000+), a rebuilt engine is a financially sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai Kona Electric engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for the electric drive unit typically takes 2 to 4 days, including high-voltage system isolation and software calibration.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a used and a rebuilt Hyundai Kona Electric engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used engine is a direct salvage pull with unknown history. A rebuilt engine is fitted with new or upgraded components and comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai Kona Electric - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Kona Electric launched, it brought accessible long-range EV motoring to the UK, powered by highly efficient permanent magnet synchronous electric motors (drive units) paired with either a 39.2 kWh or 64 kWh battery pack.

milestones.description: 100kW Electric Drive Unit (136 PS), paired with 39.2 kWh battery (Introduction of the standard-range Kona Electric).
150kW Electric Drive Unit (204 PS), paired with 64 kWh battery (Introduction of the long-range Kona Electric, offering up to 300 miles of range).
Minor software and thermal management updates to improve rapid charging speeds and battery longevity, though the core electric motor architecture remained unchanged.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every electric drive unit fitted to the Hyundai Kona Electric is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Hyundai Kona Electric Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai Kona Electric is generally highly reliable, but its electric drive unit (engine) and integrated inverter can develop specific issues over time, particularly related to thermal management and reduction gear wear. Rebuilt drive units through EnginesMarket include upgraded seals and bearings designed to address these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Inverter Coolant Leak & Reduction Gear Wear
problems.h4: Inverter Coolant Leak & Reduction Gear Wear - Why the Hyundai Kona Electric Engine Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Degradation of inverter coolant seals or reduction gear bearings due to high torque loads and thermal cycling, leading to coolant ingress or metallic whining noises from the front axle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: High-voltage isolation, inverter seal replacement, reduction gear fluid flush, and system recalibration.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for early-stage seepage; prevents catastrophic inverter or gear failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt electric drive unit with upgraded reduction gear bearings, new inverter seals, and 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if there is metallic whining, loss of propulsion, or active high-voltage fault codes.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Hyundai Kona Electric is worth £12,000-£25,000+ `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At this value, a rebuilt engine replacement cost is a small fraction of the vehicle's overall value, making replacement highly viable to preserve the asset.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is strictly an early-stage coolant seep without performance loss, a specialist seal replacement is the most cost-effective fix. However, if there is metallic whining from the reduction gear or active inverter fault codes, a fully rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the safest long-term choice for a vehicle of this caliber.

items.question: What are the signs of electric drive unit failure in a Hyundai Kona Electric?
items.answer: Early signs include a metallic whining or grinding noise from the front axle, especially under acceleration.
keyPoints: You may also notice a loss of propulsion power, inverter overheating warnings, or illuminated high-voltage system fault lights.
Ignoring these signs can lead to complete drive unit seizure.

items.answer: Yes, given the high retained value of the Kona Electric (typically £12,000-£25,000+), a rebuilt engine is a financially sound investment.

It is significantly more cost-effective than purchasing a new vehicle.

Nationwide delivery of the replacement engine can be arranged to your chosen specialist.

Rebuilt engines come with a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty, offering superior peace of mind.
